rationale:
ROUND 4 on correlation c48b7612. Round 3 was REJECTED — guardian veto on edit 4 — and the veto is UPHELD, not argued. Its reasoning, verbatim, is a better statement of the principle than anything I would write: 'This is round 3 and the code under review for edit 4 has not changed since round 2's HIGH objection — only the paperwork around it has (an architecture_review doc was filed) … Routing a scope objection to architecture review does not license deploying the disputed change … we wrote it down and routed it is not the same as it was contained.'

I had read the owner ruling of 2026-07-28 as licensing 'the code stays, file an RFC'. That ruling was an OWNER's decision about one case, not standing permission for a session to ship a disputed shared seam and write a note about it. Two seats flagged the same thing at HIGH for two consecutive rounds and I answered with a document. The seat exists to hold that line and it held it correctly.

=== WHAT CHANGED IN CODE (this is the whole of round 4) ===

1. THE VETOED CHANGE IS CONTAINED. The counting wrapper is now OPT-IN PER STEP (`copy_gate_annotate`), DEFAULT OFF, enabled only on page-content-writer's own render_section and compile_page by migration 509 — the same 'default OFF in code, the migration is the entire enablement surface' shape as migration 474. Containment is defined in the STRONG form and pinned by a test (TestAnnotationIsOffUnlessTheStepAsksForIt): a step that did not opt in cannot tell the wrapper exists — not 'it only adds keys', but 'no caller that did not ask for it can observe any difference'. WHAT IT COSTS, stated where it will be read (RFC_044 and register CQ-026): outside that one agent, 'the copy improved' and 'the check was not wired here' are the same number again. RFC_044's question flips from 'may this stay default-ON' to 'should it BECOME default-ON', and it is no longer under time pressure.

2. MIGRATION 509'S UN-HOLD CHECK WAS THE DOCUMENTED ANTI-PATTERN, and debug_historian (HIGH) was right: it read build provenance + git merge-base, but a config-backed fix ships in TWO halves — the stamp proves the BINARY and says nothing about the migration, and one `make release` resolves HEAD separately per service. It now PROBES THE CAPABILITY in the running pod (grep -ac 'rewrite_negations' /proc/1/exe) with a MANDATORY absent-control, on every replica, because a probe with no absent-control cannot distinguish 'present' from 'this grep matches anything'.

3. THE VOICE-GATE VOLUME OBJECTION (guardian edit 3, round 2 and 3) IS NOW MEASURED AND ACTED ON — and it was the objection I nearly skipped as a request for an estimate. Over the 189 live unlocked pages of the 9 sites with a voice gate: this check flags 14 pages today; x_not_y as a per-hit finding would flag 139, plus 46 for the reveal and 39 for the contrast arm. A TENFOLD FLOOD into a queue holding 45 parked voice_tells items that has had exactly ONE closed by a human — landing on another lane's queue, not mine. So the two ORIGINAL shapes stay per-hit (volume unchanged) and the three broad ones feed a page-level negation_density whose default (>12) is set from the curve: it flags 14 of 189, exactly today's volume. The check gains a new KIND of finding without gaining VOLUME. The full curve is in the code comment (8 -> 43 pages, 5 -> 61, 3 -> 87, 1 -> 150) so a site can lower it deliberately once bugs_open/033 gives that queue a working surface.

=== ANSWERED WITH EVIDENCE, NOT CHANGED ===

4. llm_reliability (medium): 'confirm IsTruncated decodes stop_reason rather than deriving from output_tokens'. IT DECODES IT: platform/aiservice/anthropic.go:420 `if response.StopReason == "max_tokens"` returns a TruncatedError with Reason 'stop_reason=max_tokens'. So the primary arm does NOT share the defaulting-to-0 gap, and the claim that it is the load-bearing protection is sound. The secondary arm's three-state fix stands regardless.
5. guidelines (medium): 'the dedup contract is DELETE+INSERT, never ON CONFLICT'. CHECKED against the platform's own audited path and the closest live precedent, and the estate does not do that: insertWorkItem uses `ON CONFLICT (site_id, item_key) WHERE item_key IS NOT NULL AND status NOT IN (<terminal list>) DO NOTHING`, and the sibling standalone check cmd/verifier-remit-check — which shipped through this council — uses a bare `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` exactly as this one does. What the seat is RIGHT about is the deeper rule the estate states in create_tool_cross_link_items.go: 'three call sites of a copied dedup rule is exactly the drift the index/Go-list contract warns about'. Minting a fourth copy of workItemTerminalStatuses in a cmd/ binary is precisely that drift (the 42P10 class), and the central helper is unexported and takes a *sql.Tx, so it is not callable here. The bare form copies no list and therefore cannot drift; that is why it stays, and the reason is now in the code rather than in this rationale.
6. reuse_agent (medium): 'the truncation three-state should be a shared helper'. Fair, and noted as the right follow-up — but deliberately NOT done in this round: the seat itself observes the fix is scoped to an arm that did not previously exist elsewhere, and extracting a helper now would mean touching other actions' truncation handling inside a round that exists to CONTAIN scope. Recorded in the lane NOTES as the next reuse step.
7. editquality (low): RFC_044 is not in the edit list. It is now edit 8.
8. improvement_guardian (low): the check files outside the discovery-check runner. Acknowledged in the seat's own words as precedented (component-fallback-check, verifier-remit-check); the anti-churn it substitutes for is the phrase-set digest key, which is stronger for this finding shape than a two-strike counter because a CHANGED brief must produce a new item rather than suppress one.

=== THE UNCHANGED CORE ===

plan.summary: Round 4 answers a guardian VETO by CONTAINING the disputed change rather than re-arguing it: the fleet-wide counting wrapper is now opt-in per step, default OFF, enabled on one agent by the held migration. edits.rationale: The family, pure and shared by every consumer so they cannot disagree about what the fault IS. Five shapes, each hit naming its containing SENTENCE with offsets into the RAW field value (a repair splices by exact substring; a sentence recovered from stripped text is not a substring of its field). ScanContrastNeighbours is a SEPARATE class that can never trip and only rejects a rewrite — without it a repair passes by moving the problem. NegationExempt is SENTENCE-scoped against brief-supplied text only, because 'rather than' is in every rendered writer prompt. AcceptNegationRewrite fails CLOSED. ROUND 2: tag comparison is now by SEQUENCE, not multiset (render_guardian: inverted nesting keeps every tag and is malformed); negative_reveal is third-person only, because the first-person form flagged 'we do not offer refunds', a policy statement the writer's own STRICT RULE 19 asks for.
edits.sketch: shapes: x_not_y | not_x_but_y | staccato | rather_than | negative_reveal neighbours (reject-only): instead_of | more_than_just | isnt_just | unlike | as_opposed_to | em_dash | … AcceptNegationRewrite(from, to, protectFrom) -> (bool, reason) empty|unchanged|gutted|ballooned|still_|displaced_|dropped_figure|invented_figure| dropped_link|markup_changed|invented_name -func sameTagMultiset(a,b) // counts equal is NOT markup preserved +func sameTagSequence(a,b) // order-equal; rejects x protectFrom = the construction's offset: facts BEFORE it are the claim and must survive; facts after it are the contrasted alternative the rewrite exists to drop.

edits.rationale: ROUND 2, and it answers bug_historian's and guardian's edit-5 objection directly: this is the traversal that was undefined at round 1. One walker for both consumers, because a repair that scanned a different set of fields from the annotation produces a count nobody can reconcile with what was fixed. It decides what counts as prose in ONE place (a cta_url or a stat value is not a sentence), returns a SORTED order because Go map order would make field paths unstable, and carries a Set closure so a repair writes through to the live map rather than into a rebuilt copy — the silent-no-op shape, designed out rather than guarded.

edits.rationale: The existing strawman arm was blind to the shape the owner complained about; it now calls the shared scanner, so the post-deploy voice check and the meta-description gate inherit the family. ONE finding per SHAPE per block carrying that shape's count — per-hit findings would flag almost every page and tell a human nothing. 'rather than' is excluded from the per-hit path and becomes a page-level DENSITY (contrast_density, default 2, long-form 4) mirroring triad_density, because it is present in 43% of sections while the house voice permits a contrasting pair once or twice per page. ROUND 4: only the two ORIGINAL shapes stay per-hit; the three broad ones feed a page-level negation_density (default >12, long-form >18) because per-hit x_not_y would take this check from 14 flagged pages to 139 of 189 on the opted-in sites — a tenfold flood into another lane's queue. The threshold is the measurement, not a preference.

edits.rationale: The repair, as its own registered action with its own input spec — not a key on execute_llm_prompt, which has 66 carriers and no spec (so the RFC_022 budget cannot see keys added to it) and also serves council seats and classifiers. ROUND 2 adds the two guards the council asked for: every candidate replacement goes through checkBannedClaims + loadEvidenceBase (the meta-description gate's own implementation, fleet arm ON) BEFORE the structural test, because 'say what it IS' is exactly the pressure that invents a superlative and nothing downstream inspects a spliced sentence for claim content; and a truncated repair splices NOTHING, detected both by aiservice.IsTruncated and by output_tokens reaching the max_tokens actually sent. Config resolution is ExecuteLLMPromptAction's own (resolveAIServiceConfig → createAIClient), so root/step overlay semantics are shared rather than re-invented. ROUND 3: the truncation second arm could not fire (output_tokens defaults to 0 when a provider reports no usage, so `>= max_tokens` was always false) — the three states are now distinct and UNKNOWN is logged rather than assumed safe. The splice already fails closed on a stale verbatim match; it is named in the sketch now.

edits.rationale: The entire enablement surface. ROUND 2 changes: renumbered 497 → 509 (497 was taken, exactly as editquality suspected); the WHERE now anchors on the CONTAINER path ...sub_workflow,steps,... so a row keyed `substeps` matches 0 rows and RAISEs rather than inserting a step nothing runs (the round-1 gating objection, which the council's own check answered as has_steps=true — the anchor makes it enforced rather than observed); a separate _HOLD_ROLLBACK file exists, with its order load-bearing (re-point first, then delete); and the header now names TWO preconditions for un-holding it, the image AND the cross-iteration budget canary. It is _HOLD because it rewires the step CHAIN: applied before the image, every section build fails at an unknown action. ROUND 4: it also enables copy_gate_annotate on this agent's own render_section and compile_page (the containment above), its verify block counts those two flags as well, the rollback clears them in the load-bearing order, and its un-hold precondition (1) now probes the CAPABILITY in the running pod with an absent-control instead of reading a build stamp.

The half the gate cannot do. The gate EXEMPTS anything the site's brief supplied — a site's voice specification outranks the fleet rules — and that is precisely the route the owner's complaint arrived by: the complained-of tagline reaches the writer in 1,369 prompts and returns in 409 responses. This asks daily whether a brief HANDS the writer such a phrase, over the writer-visible surface derived at RUNTIME from the live prompt's own {{.site_specs.specs.*}} references — never data::text, which is ~4x the text the writer reads and which made an earlier fleet census wrong by 2x. Three classes kept apart: supplied (files a finding), instructional (counted only — transfer is UNMEASURED), regulatory (left alone, by calling the SAME NegationExempt the gate uses, so the two halves cannot send a human in opposite directions). LIVE and proven: 10 of 25 sites, and the close-out arm closed two sites on positive re-observation. ROUND 3, and this is the round's most important change: the item_key was per SITE while the finding is a LIST of phrases — the documented 'key coarser than its finding' trap, which drops every finding after the first while the open row goes on describing the first thing it saw. The key now carries a digest of the sorted phrase set; close-out retires an item whose phrase set no longer describes the brief, with a reason distinguishing 'now clean' from 'the phrases changed'. Proven in production: 12 site-keyed items closed and 9 refiled under phrase-set keys in one run.

plan.risks:
1. DISPLACEMENT ADOPTED SILENTLY — the failure that would make this worse than nothing. Mitigated by per-replacement rejection against the neighbour set, with every rejection logged WITH ITS REASON. Residual: the same instinct in a grammar nobody listed. A reviewer should read the neighbour list for a shape it misses.
2. AN OVERCLAIM SPLICED IN — round 1's compliance objection. Now gated by the estate's own banned-claims scan with the fleet arm on. Residual: an overclaim no pattern names. The prompt also forbids new capability claims explicitly, which is a rule and therefore weak on its own; the scan is the control.
3. THE PER-PAGE BUDGET'S CROSS-ITERATION STATE IS UNPROVEN AT RUNTIME. Now an explicit PRECONDITION in the held migration's header rather than a follow-up canary. Degrades to per-section (headlines still repaired) if false.
4. THE 43% ARM MAY BE TOO BROAD. 'rather than' is either a real fleet tic or too wide a pattern. It is a DENSITY in the post-deploy check for that reason, and the rejection log settles it within a week of traffic. The owning lane has been asked directly.
5. COST: ~43% of sections re-asked once at ~$0.0135 (the patch shape), ~$1.2-1.7/day at 215 sections/day; with the 119 re-ask also firing, up to three calls on one section. If anyone converts this back to a whole-section re-ask it becomes ~$200/month and materially slower builds.
6. WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO: it will not clean the three pages the owner named — their tagline is brief-supplied and exempt BY DESIGN — and it holds five named FORMS rather than promising the instinct is gone. Both are stated to the owner and to the three affected lanes, in writing, before any code shipped.
7. THE SHARED-SEAM SCOPE QUESTION IS OPEN AND IS NOT THIS ROUND'S TO SETTLE: RFC_044 carries it, quoting both seats. If the architecture answer is 'declare an ActionInputSpec on both actions', that is a follow-up commit, not a change to this plan.
